questions.stem: Which statement best describes the role of an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) compared with a registered nurse in the United States?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"APRNs have essentially the same regulated scope as registered nurses because advanced education and certification do not expand clinical authority.","B":"APRNs have an identical scope in every state because state practice laws do not affect independent practice or prescribing authority.","C":"APRNs are limited to tasks delegated to assistive personnel unless a physician is physically present for each clinical decision.","D":"APRNs are educated and certified to assess, diagnose, manage problems, order tests, and prescribe within authority granted in their jurisdiction."}}
questions.rationale: NCSBN states that APRNs are educated and certified to assess, diagnose, manage patient problems, order tests, and prescribe medications, while regulatory authority can differ by jurisdiction. Option D is correct. Option A erases the advanced-practice role. Option B incorrectly claims state scopes are identical. Option C wrongly limits APRNs to assistive tasks and continuous physician presence.
questions.source_detail: Current NCSBN guidance states APRNs are prepared by education and certification to assess, diagnose and manage patient problems, order tests and prescribe medications, and notes that regulatory requirements continue to differ among jurisdictions.

qc.qc_note: Strict final audit: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; keyed option within 10% of distractor mean; keyed option is neither shortest nor longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility, grammatical parallelism, and answer-cue leakage.
